page: Microsoft Azure D64s_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, with 32 physical cores and hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes 48 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Vector Neural Network Instructions. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include any local storage or integrated GPUs, meaning all storage operations must leverage external Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities and memory performance. The server achieves a Passmark CPU score of 61,185.43 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,361.0, both placing in the top 25% tier. Large-block memory bandwidth is also highly efficient, reaching 283.92 GB/sec for read operations and 136.39 GB/sec for write operations. Multi-threaded workloads like software compilation with Clang and ray tracing show strong performance, while single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core, remain in the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, the D64s_v5 offers a balanced hardware profile suitable for enterprise-scale workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The absence of local storage represents a clear tradeoff, requiring reliance on network-attached storage, which may impact latency-sensitive I/O operations. However, the high memory bandwidth and strong multi-core processing make it highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive general-purpose applications. This server is well-suited for database operations, static web serving, multi-threaded software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications.
